title: Newcombe 1998 Table II - worked examples, difference between independent proportions
primary_reference: Newcombe RG. Interval estimation for the difference between independent proportions: comparison of eleven methods. Statistics in Medicine 1998;17(8):873-890. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19980430)17:8<873::AID-SIM779>3.0.CO;2-I

provenance.attempt_result: unreachable from the build environment: HTTP 403, 'Host not in allowlist: www.stats.org.uk'; the agent fetch path additionally fails TLS hostname verification for that host. The paywalled Wiley copy was not fetched.
provenance.actual_source: Values as reproduced in a secondary source that explicitly recasts Newcombe's Table II: 'Constructing Confidence Intervals for the Differences of Binomial Proportions', WUSS 2016 paper 127, https://www.lexjansen.com/wuss/2016/127_Final_Paper_PDF.pdf ('Table II in Newcombe (1998) provides examples for the initial 11 methods discussed above. That table is recast below...').
provenance.corroboration: Every value below is reproduced to 4 decimal places by proofpack.stats.proportions.newcombe10_bounds / newcombe11_bounds, which were written from the published formula (square-and-add of Wilson score intervals, uncorrected and continuity-corrected) and not from these numbers. An independent implementation agreeing to 4 dp on three examples spanning the interior, a boundary and a double boundary is strong evidence the transcription is right, but it is NOT a substitute for reading the paper.
provenance.action_required: Josh (or anyone with Statistics in Medicine access) should open the paper and confirm the six intervals below, then set transcribed_from_primary_pdf to true and drop the [unverified] status.
provenance.note_on_completeness: The secondary source lists three of Newcombe's worked examples. If the primary table carries more rows, add them when the paper is available; nothing in the engine depends on the row count.

method_definitions.10: score (Wilson) intervals for each proportion, combined by the square-and-add rule; no continuity correction
method_definitions.11: as method 10, built from continuity-corrected Wilson intervals

paired_examples.primary_reference: Newcombe RG. Improved confidence intervals for the difference between binomial proportions based on paired data. Statistics in Medicine 1998;17(22):2635-2650.
paired_examples.actual_source: Table III values read out of a hosted copy of the paired paper (http://www.eiti.uottawa.ca/~nat/Courses/csi5388/Newcombe.1998.pdf) by an automated fetch, not by a human reading the PDF. Same corroboration argument as above: proofpack.stats.proportions.newcombe_paired_bounds reproduces all three to 4 dp from the published formula.
paired_examples.cells: e = both positive, f = first only, g = second only, h = both negative; difference = (f - g) / n
paired_examples.method: 10 (score intervals with correlation term phi; numerator of phi continuity-corrected to max(eh - fg - n/2, 0) when eh > fg)
